passages.text: But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
passages.sermon: Jesus is the subject.\r\nJesus left the people.\r\nJesus went to the Mount of Olives.
passages.original: Ἰησοῦς δὲ ἐπορεύθη εἰς τὸ ὄρος τῶν ἐλαιῶν

passages.text: Early in the morning He went back into the temple courts. All the people came to Him, and He sat down to teach them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the subject.
Jesus is a teacher.
Early in the morning, Jesus returned to the temple courts.
All the people came to Jesus.
Jesus sat down.
Jesus taught the people.
passages.original: Ὄρθρου δὲ πάλιν παρεγένετο εἰς τὸ ἱερόν καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν καὶ καθίσας ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς

passages.text: The scribes and Pharisees, however, brought to Him a woman caught in adultery. They made her stand before them and said, “Teacher, this woman was caught in the act of adultery.
passages.sermon:
The scribes and Pharisees brought a woman to Jesus.
They had caught this woman committing adultery.
They made the woman stand in the middle of the people.
They spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Teacher, this woman was caught in the act of adultery.”
passages.original: ἄγουσιν δὲ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι πρὸς αὐτὸν γυναῖκα ἐπὶ μοιχείᾳ κατειλημμένην καὶ στήσαντες αὐτὴν ἐν μέσῳ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Διδάσκαλε αὕτη ἡ γυνὴ κατείληπται ἐπ’ αυτοφώρῳ μοιχευομένη

passages.text: In the Law Moses commanded us to stone such a woman. So what do You say?”
passages.sermon:
Moses gave us the Law.
The Law commands us to stone women like this.
What do you say?
passages.original: ἐν δὲ τῷ νόμῳ Μωϋσῆς ἡμῖν ἐνετείλατο τὰς τοιαύτας λιθάζειν σὺ οὖν τί λέγεις

passages.text: They said this to test Him, in order to have a basis for accusing Him. But Jesus bent down and began to write on the ground with His finger.
passages.sermon:
The scribes and Pharisees wanted to test Jesus.
They spoke to Him for this reason.
They wanted to find a reason to accuse Him.
Jesus bent down.
He wrote on the ground with His finger.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δὲ ἔλεγον πειράζοντες αὐτόν ἵνα ἔχωσιν κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς κάτω κύψας τῷ δακτύλῳ κατέγραφεν εἰς τὴν γῆν

passages.text: When they continued to question Him, He straightened up and said to them, “Let him who is without sin among you be the first to cast a stone at her.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood among the people.
The people questioned Jesus again and again.
They wanted Jesus to answer them.
Jesus straightened up.
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said, “If any one of you has no sin, let him be the first to throw a stone at her.”
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐπέμενον ἐρωτῶντες αὐτόν ἀνέκυψεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὁ ἀναμάρτητος ὑμῶν πρῶτος τὸν λίθον ἐπ’ αὐτῇ βαλέτω

passages.text: And again He bent down and wrote on the ground.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was present with the woman and her accusers.
He had just spoken to them.
Jesus bent down again.
He wrote on the ground with His finger.
passages.original: καὶ πάλιν κάτω¦κύψας ἔγραφεν εἰς τὴν γῆν

passages.text: When they heard this, they began to go away one by one, beginning with the older ones, until only Jesus was left, with the woman standing there.
passages.sermon:
The people heard what Jesus said.
They began to leave one by one.
The older people left first.
The others left after them.
Soon, only Jesus remained.
The woman stood there with Him.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ἐξήρχοντο εἷς καθ‿ εἷς ἀρξάμενοι ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων ἕως τῶν ἐσχάτων καὶ κατελείφθη μόνος ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἐν μέσῳ οὖσα

passages.text: Then Jesus straightened up and asked her, “Woman, where are your accusers? Has no one condemned you?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood up.
Jesus spoke to the woman.
Jesus said, “Woman, where are your accusers?”
Jesus asked, “Has no one condemned you?”
passages.original: ἀνακύψας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῇ Ἡ Γύναι ποῦ εἰσιν ἐκεῖνοι οἱ κατήγοροί σου οὐδείς σε κατέκρινεν

passages.text: “No one, Lord,” she answered. “Then neither do I condemn you,” Jesus declared. “Now go and sin no more.”
passages.sermon:
The woman answered Jesus.
She said, “No one, Lord.”
Jesus spoke to her.
Jesus said, “I do not condemn you either.”
Jesus said, “Go.”
Jesus said, “From now on, do not sin anymore.”
passages.original: Ἡ δὲ εἶπεν Οὐδείς κύριε Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐδὲ ἐγώ σε κατακρίνω πορεύου καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν μηκέτι ἁμάρτανε

passages.text: Once again, Jesus spoke to the people and said, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows Me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people again.
Jesus said, "I am the light of the world."
Anyone who follows Me will not walk in darkness.
Anyone who follows Me will have the light of life.
passages.original: Πάλιν οὖν αὐτοῖς ἐλάλησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων Ἐγώ εἰμι τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου ὁ ἀκολουθῶν ἐμοὶ οὐ μὴ περιπατήσῃ ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ ἀλλ’ ἕξει τὸ φῶς τῆς ζωῆς

passages.text: So the Pharisees said to Him, “You are testifying about Yourself; Your testimony is not valid.”
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees spoke to Jesus.
The Pharisees questioned Jesus.
They said, “You are testifying about Yourself.”
They said, “Your testimony is not valid.”
passages.original: Εἶπον οὖν αὐτῷ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι Σὺ περὶ σεαυτοῦ μαρτυρεῖς ἡ μαρτυρία σου οὐκ ἔστιν ἀληθής

passages.text: Jesus replied, “Even if I testify about Myself, My testimony is valid, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I came from or where I am going.
passages.sermon:
Jesus replied to the Pharisees.
Jesus said, "Even if I testify about Myself, My testimony is true.
I know where I came from.
I know where I am going.
You do not know where I came from.
You do not know where I am going."
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Κἂν ἐγὼ μαρτυρῶ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ ἀληθής ἐστιν ἡ μαρτυρία μου ὅτι οἶδα πόθεν ἦλθον καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγω ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ οἴδατε πόθεν ἔρχομαι ἢ ποῦ ὑπάγω

passages.text: You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees judged people by human standards.
They looked at outward things.
Jesus did not judge anyone.
Jesus did not use human standards to judge.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς κατὰ τὴν σάρκα κρίνετε ἐγὼ οὐ κρίνω οὐδένα

passages.text: But even if I do judge, My judgment is true, because I am not alone; I am with the Father who sent Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said, "If I judge, my judgment is true.
I am not alone.
The Father is with me.
The Father sent me."
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν κρίνω δὲ ἐγώ ἡ κρίσις ἡ ἐμὴ ἀληθινή ἐστιν ὅτι μόνος οὐκ εἰμί ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ πέμψας με πατήρ

passages.text: Even in your own Law it is written that the testimony of two men is valid.
passages.sermon:
Your Law is the Law of Moses.
Your Law says something important.
It says the testimony of two people is true.
It says two witnesses make a testimony valid.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐν τῷ νόμῳ δὲ τῷ ὑμετέρῳ γέγραπται ὅτι δύο ἀνθρώπων ἡ μαρτυρία ἀληθής ἐστιν

passages.text: I am One who testifies about Myself, and the Father, who sent Me, also testifies about Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus said, “I testify about Myself.
The Father sent Me.
The Father also testifies about Me.”
passages.original: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ μαρτυρῶν περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ καὶ μαρτυρεῖ περὶ ἐμοῦ ὁ πέμψας με Πατήρ

passages.text: “Where is Your Father?” they asked Him. “You do not know Me or My Father,” Jesus answered. “If you knew Me, you would know My Father as well.”
passages.sermon:
The people asked Jesus, “Where is Your Father?”
Jesus answered them.
Jesus said, “You do not know Me.
You do not know My Father.
If you knew Me, you would know My Father also.”
passages.original: Ἔλεγον οὖν αὐτῷ Ποῦ ἐστιν ὁ Πατήρ σου Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Οὔτε ἐμὲ οἴδατε οὔτε τὸν Πατέρα μου εἰ ἐμὲ ᾔδειτε καὶ τὸν Πατέρα μου ἂν ᾔδειτε

passages.text: He spoke these words while teaching in the temple courts, near the treasury. Yet no one seized Him, because His hour had not yet come.
passages.sermon:
Jesus taught in the temple.
He spoke near the treasury.
He said these words there.
No one seized Jesus.
His hour had not yet come.
passages.original: Ταῦτα τὰ ῥήματα ἐλάλησεν ἐν τῷ γαζοφυλακίῳ διδάσκων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπίασεν αὐτόν ὅτι οὔπω ἐληλύθει ἡ ὥρα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Again He said to them, “I am going away, and you will look for Me, but you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people again.
Jesus said, “I am going away.
You will look for Me.
You will die in your sin.
You cannot come where I am going.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν οὖν πάλιν αὐτοῖς Ἐγὼ ὑπάγω καὶ ζητήσετέ με καὶ ἐν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ὑμῶν ἀποθανεῖσθε ὅπου ἐγὼ ὑπάγω ὑμεῖς οὐ δύνασθε ἐλθεῖν

passages.text: So the Jews began to ask, “Will He kill Himself, since He says, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come’?”
passages.sermon:
The Jews heard Jesus speak.
Jesus said, “Where I am going, you cannot come.”
The Jews began to ask a question.
They said, “Will He kill Himself?”
They asked this because Jesus said, “Where I am going, you cannot come.”
passages.original: Ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι Μήτι ἀποκτενεῖ ἑαυτὸν ὅτι λέγει Ὅπου ἐγὼ ὑπάγω ὑμεῖς οὐ δύνασθε ἐλθεῖν

passages.text: Then He told them, “You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
He said, "You are from below.
I am from above.
You belong to this world.
I do not belong to this world."
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ὑμεῖς ἐκ τῶν κάτω ἐστέ ἐγὼ ἐκ τῶν ἄνω εἰμί ὑμεῖς ἐκ τούτου τοῦ κόσμου ἐστέ ἐγὼ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου τούτου

passages.text: That is why I told you that you would die in your sins. For unless you believe that I am He, you will die in your sins.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Jews.
Jesus said, "You will die in your sins.
I told you this before.
If you do not believe that I am He,
You will die in your sins."
passages.original: εἶπον οὖν ὑμῖν ὅτι ἀποθανεῖσθε ἐν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ὑμῶν ἐὰν γὰρ μὴ πιστεύσητε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι ἀποθανεῖσθε ἐν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ὑμῶν

passages.text: “Who are You?” they asked. “Just what I have been telling you from the beginning,” Jesus replied.
passages.sermon:
The people spoke to Jesus.
They asked Him, "Who are You?"
Jesus answered them.
Jesus said, "I am the same One I have told you about from the beginning."
Jesus had already told them who He was.
passages.original: Ἔλεγον οὖν αὐτῷ Σὺ τίς εἶ Εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Τὴν ἀρχὴν ὅ¦τι καὶ λαλῶ ὑμῖν

passages.text: “I have much to say about you and much to judge. But the One who sent Me is truthful, and what I have heard from Him, I tell the world.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said, “I have many things to say about you.
I have many things to judge about you.
The One who sent Me is truthful.
I speak to the world what I heard from Him.”
passages.original: πολλὰ ἔχω περὶ ὑμῶν λαλεῖν καὶ κρίνειν ἀλλ’ ὁ πέμψας με ἀληθής ἐστιν κἀγὼ ἃ ἤκουσα παρ’ αὐτοῦ ταῦτα λαλῶ εἰς τὸν κόσμον

passages.text: They did not understand that He was telling them about the Father.
passages.sermon: The people did not understand Jesus.\r\nJesus spoke about the Father.\r\nThe people did not realize this.
passages.original: Οὐκ ἔγνωσαν ὅτι τὸν Πατέρα αὐτοῖς ἔλεγεν

passages.text: So Jesus said, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am He, and that I do nothing on My own, but speak exactly what the Father has taught Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
He said, "You will lift up the Son of Man."
When you lift up the Son of Man, you will know that I am He.
I do nothing by Myself.
I speak only what the Father has taught Me.
I do not act on My own.
I say what the Father taught Me.
passages.original: εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ὅταν ὑψώσητε τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τότε γνώσεσθε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι καὶ ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ ποιῶ οὐδέν ἀλλὰ καθὼς ἐδίδαξέν με ὁ Πατὴρ ταῦτα λαλῶ

passages.text: He who sent Me is with Me. He has not left Me alone, because I always do what pleases Him.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about Himself.
God the Father sent Jesus.
God is with Jesus.
God has not left Jesus alone.
Jesus always does what pleases God.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ πέμψας με μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν οὐκ ἀφῆκέν με μόνον ὅτι ἐγὼ τὰ ἀρεστὰ αὐτῷ ποιῶ πάντοτε

passages.text: As Jesus spoke these things, many believed in Him.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke these things.\r\nMany people listened to Jesus.\r\nMany people believed in Jesus.
passages.original: Ταῦτα αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν

passages.text: So He said to the Jews who had believed Him, “If you continue in My word, you are truly My disciples.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Jews who had believed Him.
He said, "If you continue in My word, you are truly My disciples."
You must remain faithful to My teaching.
If you do this, you show that you are really My followers.
passages.original: Ἔλεγεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς τοὺς πεπιστευκότας αὐτῷ Ἰουδαίους Ἐὰν ὑμεῖς μείνητε ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τῷ ἐμῷ ἀληθῶς μαθηταί μού ἐστε

passages.text: Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the Jews who believed in Him.\r\nHe said, “You will know the truth.\r\nThe truth will set you free.”
passages.original: καὶ γνώσεσθε τὴν ἀλήθειαν καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια ἐλευθερώσει ὑμᾶς

passages.text: “We are Abraham’s descendants,” they answered. “We have never been slaves to anyone. How can You say we will be set free?”
passages.sermon:
The Jews who believed Jesus spoke to Him.
They answered Jesus.
They said, “We are Abraham’s descendants.”
They said, “We have never been slaves to anyone.”
They asked Jesus, “How can You say we will be set free?”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν πρὸς αὐτόν Σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ ἐσμεν καὶ οὐδενὶ δεδουλεύκαμεν πώποτε πῶς σὺ λέγεις ὅτι Ἐλεύθεροι γενήσεσθε

passages.text: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, everyone who sins is a slave to sin.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to them.\r\nHe said, “I tell you the truth.\r\nEveryone who commits sin is a slave to sin.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ποιῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν δοῦλός ἐστιν τῆς ἁμαρτίας

passages.text: A slave is not a permanent member of the family, but a son belongs to it forever.
passages.sermon:
A slave does not stay in the family forever.
A slave is not a permanent member of the family.
A son stays in the family forever.
A son belongs to the family always.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ δοῦλος οὐ μένει ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ὁ υἱὸς μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα

passages.text: So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.
passages.sermon: Jesus is the Son of God.\r\nJesus has the power to set people free.\r\nIf Jesus sets you free, you will truly be free.
passages.original: ἐὰν οὖν ὁ Υἱὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλευθερώσῃ ὄντως ἐλεύθεροι ἔσεσθε

passages.text: I know you are Abraham’s descendants, but you are trying to kill Me because My word has no place within you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus knew they were descendants of Abraham.
Jesus said they were trying to kill Him.
Jesus said His word had no place within them.
passages.original: Οἶδα ὅτι σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ ἐστε ἀλλὰ ζητεῖτέ με ἀποκτεῖναι ὅτι ὁ λόγος ὁ ἐμὸς οὐ χωρεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν

passages.text: I speak of what I have seen in the presence of the Father, and you do what you have heard from your father.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus has seen things while with the Father.
Jesus speaks about what he has seen with the Father.
The people have a different father.
The people do what they have heard from their father.
passages.original: ἃ ἐγὼ ἑώρακα παρὰ τῷ Πατρὶ λαλῶ καὶ ὑμεῖς οὖν ἃ ἠκούσατε παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ποιεῖτε

passages.text: “Abraham is our father,” they replied. “If you were children of Abraham,” said Jesus, “you would do the works of Abraham.
passages.sermon:
The people spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Abraham is our father.”
Jesus answered them.
Jesus said, “If you were truly Abraham’s children, you would do what Abraham did.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ὁ πατὴρ ἡμῶν Ἀβραάμ ἐστιν Λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Εἰ τέκνα τοῦ Ἀβραάμ ἐστε τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ ἐποιεῖτε

passages.text: But now you are trying to kill Me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham never did such a thing.
passages.sermon:
You are trying to kill Me now.
I am a man.
I have told you the truth.
I heard this truth from God.
Abraham did not do this.
Abraham never tried to kill someone who told the truth from God.
passages.original: νῦν δὲ ζητεῖτέ με ἀποκτεῖναι ἄνθρωπον ὃς τὴν ἀλήθειαν ὑμῖν λελάληκα ἣν ἤκουσα παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦτο Ἀβραὰμ οὐκ ἐποίησεν

passages.text: You are doing the works of your father.” “We are not illegitimate children,” they declared. “Our only Father is God Himself.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said, "You are doing the works of your father."
The people answered Jesus.
They said, "We are not illegitimate children."
They said, "God is our only Father."
passages.original: ὑμεῖς ποιεῖτε τὰ ἔργα τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν Εἶπαν οὖν αὐτῷ Ἡμεῖς ἐκ πορνείας οὐ γεγεννήμεθα ἕνα Πατέρα ἔχομεν τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: Jesus said to them, “If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I have come here from God. I have not come on My own, but He sent Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus said, "If God were your Father, you would love Me.
I came from God.
I am here because God sent Me.
I did not come by Myself.
God sent Me."
passages.original: Εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Εἰ ὁ Θεὸς Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἦν ἠγαπᾶτε ἂν ἐμέ ἐγὼ γὰρ ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐξῆλθον καὶ ἥκω οὐδὲ γὰρ ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ ἐλήλυθα ἀλλ’ ἐκεῖνός με ἀπέστειλεν

passages.text: Why do you not understand what I am saying? It is because you are unable to accept My message.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He asked them a question.
He said, "Why do you not understand what I am saying?"
He gave the reason.
He said, "You are unable to accept My message."
passages.original: Διὰ τί τὴν λαλιὰν τὴν ἐμὴν οὐ γινώσκετε ὅτι οὐ δύνασθε ἀκούειν τὸν λόγον τὸν ἐμόν

passages.text: You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to carry out his desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
passages.sermon:
You belong to your father, the devil.
You want to do what your father desires.
The devil was a murderer from the beginning.
He has never stood in the truth.
There is no truth in him.
When the devil lies, he speaks from his own nature.
He is a liar.
He is the father of lies.
passages.original: ὑμεῖς ἐκ τοῦ πατρὸς τοῦ διαβόλου ἐστὲ καὶ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν θέλετε ποιεῖν ἐκεῖνος ἀνθρωποκτόνος ἦν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ οὐκ ἔστηκεν ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ἀλήθεια ἐν αὐτῷ ὅταν λαλῇ τὸ ψεῦδος ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων λαλεῖ ὅτι ψεύστης ἐστὶν καὶ ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me!
passages.sermon: I speak the truth.\r\nYou do not believe Me because I speak the truth.
passages.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ὅτι τὴν ἀλήθειαν λέγω οὐ πιστεύετέ μοι

passages.text: Which of you can prove Me guilty of sin? If I speak the truth, why do you not believe Me?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus asked a question.
He said, "Can any of you prove that I am guilty of sin?"
He said, "I speak the truth."
He asked, "Why do you not believe Me?"
passages.original: Τίς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἐλέγχει με περὶ ἁμαρτίας εἰ ἀλήθειαν λέγω διὰ τί ὑμεῖς οὐ πιστεύετέ μοι

passages.text: Whoever belongs to God hears the words of God. The reason you do not hear is that you do not belong to God.”
passages.sermon: A person who belongs to God hears the words of God.\r\nYou do not hear the words of God.\r\nYou do not belong to God.
passages.original: ὁ ὢν ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ τὰ ῥήματα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀκούει διὰ τοῦτο ὑμεῖς οὐκ ἀκούετε ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐκ ἐστέ

passages.text: The Jews answered Him, “Are we not right to say that You are a Samaritan and You have a demon?”
passages.sermon:
The Jews spoke to Jesus.
They answered Him.
They said, “Are we right to say this about you?
You are a Samaritan.
You have a demon.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Οὐ καλῶς λέγομεν ἡμεῖς ὅτι Σαμαρίτης εἶ σὺ καὶ δαιμόνιον ἔχεις

passages.text: “I do not have a demon,” Jesus replied, “but I honor My Father, and you dishonor Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus replied to the Jews.
Jesus said, “I do not have a demon.
I honor My Father.
You dishonor Me.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Ἐγὼ δαιμόνιον οὐκ ἔχω ἀλλὰ τιμῶ τὸν Πατέρα μου καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀτιμάζετέ με

passages.text: I do not seek My own glory. There is One who seeks it, and He is the Judge.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to the Jews.
\r\nJesus does not seek His own glory.
\r\nGod seeks the glory of Jesus.
\r\nGod is the Judge.
passages.original: ἐγὼ δὲ οὐ ζητῶ τὴν δόξαν μου ἔστιν ὁ ζητῶν καὶ κρίνων

passages.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, if anyone keeps My word, he will never see death.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus said, “Truly, truly, I tell you.”
If anyone keeps My word, he will never see death.
This means that those who obey Jesus will not experience death forever.
passages.original: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἐάν τις τὸν ἐμὸν λόγον τηρήσῃ θάνατον οὐ μὴ θεωρήσῃ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα

passages.text: “Now we know that You have a demon!” declared the Jews. “Abraham died, and so did the prophets, yet You say that anyone who keeps Your word will never taste death.
passages.sermon:
The Jews spoke to Jesus.
They said, “Now we know you have a demon.”
Abraham died.
The prophets also died.
You say, ‘If anyone keeps my word, he will never taste death.’”
passages.original: Εἶπον οὖν αὐτῷ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι Νῦν ἐγνώκαμεν ὅτι δαιμόνιον ἔχεις Ἀβραὰμ ἀπέθανεν καὶ οἱ προφῆται καὶ σὺ λέγεις Ἐάν τις τὸν λόγον μου τηρήσῃ οὐ μὴ γεύσηται θανάτου εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα

passages.text: Are You greater than our father Abraham? He died, as did the prophets. Who do You claim to be?”
passages.sermon:
The Jews spoke to Jesus.
They asked Jesus a question.
They said, "Are you greater than our father Abraham?"
Abraham died.
The prophets also died.
They asked, "Who do you claim to be?"
passages.original: μὴ σὺ μείζων εἶ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἀβραάμ ὅστις ἀπέθανεν καὶ οἱ προφῆται ἀπέθανον τίνα σεαυτὸν ποιεῖς

passages.text: Jesus answered, “If I glorify Myself, My glory means nothing. The One who glorifies Me is My Father, of whom you say ‘He is our God.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Jews.
Jesus answered their question.
Jesus said, "If I glorify Myself, My glory means nothing."
My Father is the One who glorifies Me.
You say that He is your God.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Ἐὰν ἐγὼ δοξάσω ἐμαυτόν ἡ δόξα μου οὐδέν ἐστιν ἔστιν ὁ Πατήρ μου ὁ δοξάζων με ὃν ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι Θεὸς ἡμῶν ἐστιν

passages.text: You do not know Him, but I know Him. If I said I did not know Him, I would be a liar like you. But I do know Him, and I keep His word.
passages.sermon:
You do not know God.
I know God.
If I said I do not know God, I would be a liar like you.
But I do know God.
I keep His word.
passages.original: καὶ οὐκ ἐγνώκατε αὐτόν ἐγὼ δὲ οἶδα αὐτόν κἂν εἴπω ὅτι οὐκ οἶδα αὐτόν ἔσομαι ὅμοιος ὑμῖν ψεύστης ἀλλὰ οἶδα αὐτὸν καὶ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ τηρῶ

passages.text: Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see My day. He saw it and was glad.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham is your father.
Abraham looked forward to seeing My day.
Abraham rejoiced because of this hope.
Abraham saw My day.
Abraham was glad.
passages.original: Ἀβραὰμ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἠγαλλιάσατο ἵνα ἴδῃ τὴν ἡμέραν τὴν ἐμήν καὶ εἶδεν καὶ ἐχάρη

passages.text: Then the Jews said to Him, “You are not yet fifty years old, and You have seen Abraham?”
passages.sermon: The Jews spoke to Jesus.\r\nThey said, “You are not yet fifty years old.”\r\nThey asked, “Have you seen Abraham?”
passages.original: Εἶπον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι πρὸς αὐτόν Πεντήκοντα ἔτη οὔπω ἔχεις καὶ Ἀβραὰμ ἑώρακας

passages.text: “Truly, truly, I tell you,” Jesus declared, “before Abraham was born, I am!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus said, “Truly, truly, I tell you.”
Jesus said, “I existed before Abraham was born.”
Jesus said, “I am.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν πρὶν Ἀβραὰμ γενέσθαι ἐγὼ εἰμί

passages.text: At this, they picked up stones to throw at Him. But Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple area.
passages.sermon:
The Jews became angry at Jesus.
They picked up stones.
They wanted to throw the stones at Jesus.
Jesus hid Himself.
Jesus left the temple area.
passages.original: Ἦραν οὖν λίθους ἵνα βάλωσιν ἐπ’ αὐτόν Ἰησοῦς δὲ ἐκρύβη καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ
